item.title: Woman injured in Ticino: arrest for attempted murder
item.description: A 28-year-old Romanian citizen was arrested on October 9 after a domestic dispute in Ticino.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - A 28-year-old Romanian citizen was arrested on October 9 - The altercation took place in a domestic setting - The woman's injuries required a hospital visit - The injuries did not endanger her life
## Key facts - Place → Canton Ticino - Arrested person → 28-year-old Romanian citizen - Residence → Romania - Date of arrest → October 9 - Nature of the dispute → domestic - Injuries → hospital visit - Danger to life → not in danger
On October 9, in Canton Ticino, a 28-year-old Romanian citizen residing in Romania was arrested. The news was made public by the cantonal police, which reported that the arrest was carried out by officers from the Lugano City Police and the cantonal police.
The intervention followed a dispute that had previously occurred in a domestic setting. During the dispute, a woman sustained injuries that required a hospital visit. The source clarifies, however, that the injuries were not such as to endanger her life.
The available reconstruction is limited to these elements: a domestic incident, the woman's injury, the intervention by police forces, and the man's arrest. No other details are provided about the dynamics of the dispute, nor are statements by the arrested man or the woman reported.
The arrest is therefore the central fact communicated by the cantonal police in a case being treated as attempted murder. The measure concerns a Romanian citizen residing in Romania, while the location indicated for the incident is only the domestic setting. The source does not specify the address or municipality where the dispute occurred.
The news also distinguishes the alleged offense from the medical outcome: the injuries resulted in a hospital visit, but not a danger to life. This is the factual picture made public along with the announcement of the arrest. ## The alleged offences
The text first indicates attempted intentional homicide. Alongside this allegation, the source reports, in the alternative, attempted grievous bodily harm and, in the further alternative, simple bodily harm. The charges also include an infringement of the Federal Act on Foreign Nationals.
The list is provided by the cantonal police in the statement on the arrest and represents the alleged offences indicated in connection with the incident. The published text does not provide any further description of what happened or of the reasons why the different legal classifications were formulated. For this reason, the report is limited to listing the charges as communicated.
### The woman's condition
On the health front, the available information is limited. The woman sustained injuries during the altercation and needed a hospital visit. The source adds one precise detail about the outcome: the injuries were not such as to endanger her life.
Attempted intentional homicide is the first allegation listed, followed by the alternative allegations of attempted grievous bodily harm and simple bodily harm. The same statement includes the infringement of the Federal Act on Foreign Nationals, without adding any further details about its content.
The case therefore remains described through two aspects present in the source: the injuries that required hospital treatment and the set of alleged offences indicated in the statement. No further assessment is included in the available text. ## The continuation of the investigation
The source indicates as a development that has already taken place the confirmation of the restrictive measure of liberty by the Judge of Coercive Measures, the GPC. This step is reported as having occurred in the meantime following the arrest.
The investigation is coordinated by Public Prosecutor Veronica Lipari. The statement therefore identifies the GPC as the body that confirmed the measure and Veronica Lipari as the public prosecutor coordinating the investigation. These are the procedural elements made available in the text.
### The procedural elements
The statement does not add a date for any possible hearing, does not indicate any other decisions by the GPC, and does not report any statements by the prosecutor. Nor does it report any further stages of the investigation. The available information on what follows is therefore limited to confirmation of the restrictive measure and coordination of the investigation by Veronica Lipari.
These two pieces of information define the procedural status described by the source: the restrictive measure of liberty is confirmed, while the investigation is coordinated by the indicated Public Prosecutor. The cantonal police announcement provides no further details on the timing or subsequent measures.
As regards the public follow-up to the matter, the text therefore makes it possible to record only what has already been communicated: confirmation of the measure by the GPC and the name of the prosecutor coordinating the investigation.

item.title: Accused of murder, arrested in Como for extradition
item.description: A 40-year-old man was arrested in Como.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - A 40-year-old man arrested in Como. - Identified on via Canturina by the State Police. - Pakistan had requested his extradition. - The alleged murder took place in 2023. ## Key facts - Age → 40 years old - Where → via Canturina, Como - Checks → combating illegal immigration - Request → international arrest warrant for extradition - Offense → murder committed in Pakistan in 2023 Yesterday afternoon, the Como State Police arrested a 40-year-old man during routine checks aimed at combating illegal immigration. Officers found and identified him on via Canturina, in Como. Checks revealed that the 40-year-old was subject to an international measure aimed at extradition, requested by the Pakistani authorities. The measure is related to proceedings concerning a murder that took place in Pakistan in 2023. The source reports that the man had become untraceable during the hearings in which he was standing trial for that murder. Following the checks carried out by the officers, he was arrested. The check thus led to the inquiries that preceded the measure requested by the Pakistani authorities. ## The proceedings referred to in the request The judicial case mentioned in the identification in Como is connected to Pakistan. The source indicates that the murder took place in 2023 and that the forty-year-old man was charged in the related proceedings. During the hearings, however, he had become untraceable. This is the passage that explains the presence of an international arrest request for extradition purposes. It was submitted by the Pakistani authorities, while officers of the State Police in Como verified the man's identity and the presence of the international request during checks on via Canturina. The text keeps the details limited: it does not specify the dynamics of the murder, does not report statements by the defendant and does not describe the content of the hearings. What remains indicated are the country of the proceedings, the year of the incident, the murder charge and the man's untraceability during the hearings. These are the elements linking the check carried out in Como to the international procedure requested by Pakistan. ## Transfer to Bassone At the end of the checks, the officers arrested the man and took him to Bassone Prison. The source places this step after the discovery and identification on via Canturina and after verification of the international request for extradition. The forty-year-old man is now at the disposal of the Milan Court of Appeal, indicated as competent for the extradition procedure. This is the judicial authority called upon to follow the procedure described in the news report, while the initial request was submitted by the Pakistani authorities. The reported developments stop at the arrest, the transfer to prison and placing him at the disposal of the Milan Court of Appeal. The text precisely indicates the place of transfer, Bassone Prison, and the competent authority, the Milan Court of Appeal. The next phase is the extradition procedure. *Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/cronaca/accusato-di-omicidio-fugge-dal-pakistan-fermato-dalla-polizia-a-como-sara-estradato/)*

item.description: 26-year-old Russian citizen arrested Garage window damaged Attempted escape after detention Como prison awaiting immediate trial What →

## TL;DR - Arrested a 26-year-old Russian citizen - The glass window of a garage was damaged - Attempted escape after being detained - Como prison pending immediate trial ## Key facts - What → unauthorized entry into the Fire Brigade headquarters - Where → via Valleggio, Como - When → Wednesday afternoon, around 15.00 - Who → 26-year-old Russian citizen - Outcome → transfer to Como prison Yesterday afternoon, Wednesday, the Como State Police arrested a 26-year-old Russian citizen with no fixed address in Italy and irregular status in the country. The man had unlawfully entered the headquarters of the Fire Brigade Command on via Valleggio, in Como. The report also mentions some damage, including the glass window of a garage. ### The report and initial response Around 15.00, officers from the police headquarters patrol unit arrived at the Fire Brigade Command headquarters after being informed that someone was inside the facility. Before the police arrived, the personnel on site had restrained the 26-year-old following the damage. The patrol then took custody of the man, who was found to be agitated. During a personal search, the Russian citizen immediately showed little cooperation. He then had an outburst of anger in the service vehicle and attempted to escape. The officers promptly restrained him. The sequence described therefore begins with the unauthorized presence at the headquarters, continues with the reported damage, and culminates in the attempt to evade control after being detained. The initial response took place entirely in Como and involved the headquarters on via Valleggio, Fire Brigade personnel and officers from the police headquarters patrol unit. At this stage, the source places the unauthorized entry, the damaged glass window and the attempted escape before the further checks carried out by the State Police. ## Checks at Police Headquarters ### Identification and behavior The attempted escape did not result in the man getting away. In an attempt to break free from the officers, the 26-year-old kicked and punched one of the officers. The officers restrained him and then took him to Police Headquarters for fingerprint and photographic identification checks and the customary checks. The checks uncovered several aliases, as well as various offenses related to immigration regulations and offenses against public administration, in addition to criminal convictions. The identification therefore added to the elements of the intervention the results of the checks carried out in the Police Headquarters offices. Even while in the holding cells, the detainee maintained an aggressive attitude. This behavior was observed while he was still in police custody, before medical personnel intervened. Because the 26-year-old was highly agitated, the officers called in medical personnel. The request was made while the 26-year-old was in the holding cells. The part of the incident following his being taken into custody therefore includes physical contact with one of the officers, the restraint, being taken to Police Headquarters, and the carrying out of the checks. During the same period, the aliases coming to light, the offenses indicated, the criminal convictions reported in the account, and the aggressive behavior that led to the request for medical assistance all occurred. The checks and the time spent in the holding cells are described before the medical intervention. The detainee's time at Police Headquarters therefore had a dual purpose: identification, through fingerprint and photographic checks, and management of the detainee, because of the attitude he maintained in the holding cells. ## The arrest and the wait for the fast-track trial ### The charges The medical staff, responding at the officers' request, calmed the 26-year-old and transported him to a hospital. Following this, the Russian citizen was arrested. The report cites as grounds for the arrest aggravated property damage, violence, threats, resistance and injury to a public official, disruption of a public service, defacement and unlawful entry, as well as resistance to a public official. The list brings together the offenses reported by Como State Police concerning the incident that took place at the Fire Brigade headquarters. The wording includes aggravated property damage; in the reconstruction of the intervention, the garage's glass window is mentioned among the damage. Unlawful entry, disruption of a public service and defacement are also listed, together with the charges of violence, threats, resistance and injury to a public official and resistance to a public official. ### Custody in Como By order of the judicial authority, the 26-year-old was committed to Como prison. This committal came after the transfer to hospital and after the arrest for the offenses listed in the report. The destination indicated is therefore Como prison, where the man was transferred while awaiting the fast-track trial. The final sequence reported is that of the medical intervention, the arrest and the subsequent order of the judicial authority. The follow-up indicated by the source is awaiting the fast-track trial and the arrested man's remaining in Como prison. Como prison is therefore where the 26-year-old was committed after the order of the judicial authority, while the fast-track trial remains the proceeding awaited at the stage described. *Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/entra-abusivamente-nellautorimessa-del-comando-dei-vigili-del-fuoco-arrestato-a-como-dalla-polizia/2709043/)*

item.title: SSR cuts another 202 jobs
item.description: SSR is eliminating 202 full-time positions and expects savings of 41 million.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - SSR cuts another 202 full-time positions - 173 reductions concern the Operations sector - The measure enables savings of 41 million francs - Around 270 million francs in savings are needed by 2029
Total cuts → 202 full-time positions Operations sector → 173 positions Other sectors → 29 positions Savings from the measure → 41 million francs 2027 target → 80 million francs 2029 target → around 270 million francs RSI → up to 12 fewer positions in 2027
SSR announced on Thursday the elimination of another 202 full-time jobs. The decision includes 173 cuts in Operations. The other 29 positions concern Human Resources, Finance, Communication & Public Affairs and Staff.
The measure will enable Società svizzera di radiotelevisione to save 41 million francs. The measure is part of recent political decisions, including the reduction of the license fee to 300 francs. As a result of these choices, the company is required to save around 270 million by 2029, of which 80 million already in 2027. The figure of 41 million concerns this measure, while the other amounts indicate overall targets over different time horizons.
### The section on 2027 With the measures announced last month for the regional units RSI, RTR, RTS and SRF, SSR says it has fully realized the savings planned for 2027. For RSI, the figure indicated is a reduction of up to 12 positions in 2027. The source does not specify the distribution of the positions among locations, functions or categories of workers.
The categories do not have the same numerical weight: 173 positions are concentrated in Operations, while 29 are distributed among the four areas listed. The text does not provide an internal breakdown of the 29 and does not assign the 202 to individual locations. The overall figure refers to full-time jobs, without a list of people or duties involved.
Personnel management will, where possible, rely on natural turnover and retirements. According to SSR, this approach will absorb around half of the reductions in Operations and support sectors. However, it will not be enough to avoid all the effects: layoffs and early retirements are described as inevitable. The company will apply its social plan.
For those who live near the border and work in Ticino, the verifiable fact is therefore a reorganization that also includes RSI; it is not possible, however, to determine from the source how many cross-border workers are involved or which individual conditions will change. The text stops at the overall numbers, company areas and timing of the savings. ## For the cross-border worker, the actual scope of the news
A cross-border worker who works for SSR, or is considering a job connected with RSI, can use the news to identify organizational risk, not to automatically calculate a change in their paycheck. The text refers to positions being eliminated, savings and personnel management; it does not indicate salaries, working hours, locations, individual contracts or criteria for choosing the people affected. The overall figure of 202 therefore cannot be turned into a figure for cross-border workers.
The first comparison concerns the areas: 173 positions are in Operations, 29 in support sectors. A role falling within one of these areas is not described as automatically eliminated. The source does not provide a list of functions, nor does it distinguish between employees residing in Switzerland and cross-border workers. The RSI figure is also phrased as up to 12 fewer positions in 2027: it is not a description of individual positions and contains no names or locations.
For readers in Canton Ticino, the practical angle therefore remains employment-related. The source does not announce changes to the G permit, AVS, LPP or LAMal. It does not address tax rebates, withholding tax, INPS, Brogeda or double taxation. These elements cannot be inferred from SSR's savings plan, because the text does not link them to the reorganization.
The difference between natural attrition and imposed departures is the second point to consider. SSR states that natural turnover and retirements will cover, as far as possible, about half of the reductions in the sectors indicated. It adds, however, that dismissals and early retirements are unavoidable and that the social plan will be applied. Without details about the plan, it is not possible to calculate compensation, timelines or conditions for an individual cross-border worker.
The timetable has two levels: 80 million in savings already in 2027 and around 270 million by 2029. These are company targets, not individual deadlines. The source does not indicate dates for personal communications, nor a different procedure for those crossing the border. The cross-border worker cannot infer from these figures an automatic change in their permit, social security or taxation.
The before-and-after comparison is therefore limited: the source does not provide a previous snapshot of the number of employees by area, but it discloses the overall volume of the cuts, the main breakdown and the savings horizon. The figure serves to clarify the direction of the reorganization, not to anticipate the outcome of every employment relationship. ## How to use the information
The source does not describe an individual procedure for employees or indicate forms, offices or personal deadlines. To avoid conflating company data with personal circumstances, a worker can follow a five-step reading, all based on the published information.
1. Separate the scope. Note that the measure concerns 202 full-time positions and that the largest share, 173, is in Operations. The remaining 29 are associated with the four areas listed: Human Resources, Finance, Communications & Public Affairs and Staff.
2. Isolate the RSI figure. Note separately the wording up to 12 fewer positions in 2027. That “up to” indicates a threshold reported by the source; it does not justify turning it into a certain number of people or a list of roles.
3. Separate the timelines. 2027 is the time horizon for the first 80 million in savings and for the measures already implemented for the regional units; 2029 is the deadline indicated for approximately 270 million. These are two distinct company references.
4. Distinguish the methods. Note that natural attrition and retirements absorb, as far as possible, about half of the reductions in Operations and the support sectors. However, the same communication points to unavoidable layoffs and early retirements and the implementation of the social plan.
5. Stop at the available data. The text does not provide individual criteria, departure dates, social plan amounts, locations or names. It therefore does not make it possible to calculate the personal impact for a cross-border worker, or to infer effects on withholding tax, AVS or other institutions not mentioned.
For those who work across the border, this method avoids two opposite errors: reading the 202 positions as if they were all in RSI, or treating the up to 12 RSI positions as a list of names. The source makes it possible to follow the scope of the savings and the stated methods, but it does not contain an individual communication from the company. Since no personal forms, offices or deadlines are indicated, adding them would mean going beyond the available data.

Three men were arrested in the Mendrisiotto last Wednesday: two Slovaks aged 39 and 28 and a 30-year-old Czech, all residing in their respective countries of origin. The three are suspected of having participated in scams targeting elderly people through the so-called “shock calls.”

On Wednesday, in Chiasso, staff from the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security located the trio’s vehicle, finding cash and valuables inside.

item.description: 2027 deficit: 14,7 million francs Net planned investments: 97 million Confirmed multipliers: 80% and 85% Subject → City of Lugano Decision →
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 2027 deficit: 14,7 million francs - Expected net investments: 97 million - Multipliers confirmed: 80% and 85%
## Key facts - Subject → City of Lugano - Decision → approved by the Municipal Executive - Next review → City Council - Ordinary expenses → 510,8 million francs - Ordinary revenue → 224,1 million francs - Tax requirement → 286,7 million francs - Tax revenue from individuals → 221 million francs - Tax revenue from legal entities → 51 million francs
## A smaller deficit The Municipal Executive has given the green light to the 2027 Budget of the City of Lugano, which now goes to the City Council for review and approval. The accounts remain in the red, but the deficit is lower than in previous projections. The forecast points to a loss of 14,7 million francs, 4,8 million less than the 19,5 million included for the same year in the 2026-2033 Financial Plan.
The comparison with the previous multi-year projection makes the adjustment more evident: at that time, the estimated deficit was 30,1 million, thus 15,4 million higher than now forecast. For the Municipal Executive, this figure confirms the financial recovery path undertaken. It does not, however, close the matter: the Executive points out that further measures will be needed to bring the accounts back toward a lasting balance.
### Budget items As regards ordinary operations, the document sets out expenses of 510,8 million francs and revenue of 224,1 million. The amount to be covered through taxation is given as 286,7 million. Estimated tax revenue amounts to 221 million from individuals and 51 million from legal entities.
The Municipal Executive is keeping the two tax multipliers unchanged: 80% for individuals and 85% for legal entities. The choice is linked to the desire to continue rebalancing without increasing the tax burden through the multipliers and to preserve the city's attractiveness for residents and businesses.
The plan also provides for 97 million in net investment in 2027. The sum includes the deferred payment of part of the balance due for the purchase of PalaRaiffeisen. Self-financing is estimated at 16,6 million, while the overall result comes to negative 80,4 million. The same presentation therefore highlights the need to monitor the evolution of debt and the sustainability of investments.
### The 2026 update The Municipal Executive also announced that the projected closing of financial year 2026 is expected to result in a surplus in current operations. The signal is positive, but it does not amount to a structural rebalancing of the city's finances, which will still require time and further measures. The Budget incorporates the recovery measures already decided by the Executive and requested by the City Council. It does not, however, include the measures needed to offset from 2028 the financial consequences of the popular votes held in 2025, according to current financial planning. ## What changes, and what remains outside The confirmation of the multipliers should be read separately from the overall result. For individuals, the multiplier remains at 80%, while for legal entities it remains at 85%, as indicated by the City for 2027. The decision does not eliminate the projected deficit, but avoids pursuing rebalancing through an increase in the multipliers. This is the rationale the Municipal Council links to protecting attractiveness for residents and businesses.
The second element concerns the difference between an improvement in estimates and a return to balance. Moving from a projection of 30,1 million to a projected deficit of 14,7 million represents a significant correction, but the budget remains negative. Any surplus in current operations in 2026 should therefore be regarded as a positive signal regarding the closing of the financial year, not as the solution already achieved for the overall financial picture.
For those reading as cross-border commuters, the news has a precise scope: the source does not address a G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax refunds, INPS or double taxation, and does not present any changes to withholding tax. The content concerns the financial management of the City of Lugano and not a procedure concerning cross-border work.
### Three comparisons to keep separate | Comparison | Source data | Interpretation | | 2027 | Deficit of 14,7 million | Still-negative forecast | | 2026-2033 financial plan | 19,5 million for 2027 | Higher previous estimate | | Previous multi-year projection | 30,1 million | Even more unfavorable picture | | 2026 financial year | Expected surplus in current operations | Positive indication regarding the closing |
The same prudence applies to investments. The 97 million net also include the deferred payment of part of the balance for PalaRaiffeisen. Alongside this figure, the document indicates 16,6 million in self-financing and an overall result of minus 80,4 million. For the Municipal Council, the data as a whole make it necessary to continue monitoring indebtedness and the sustainability of investments.
Finally, the financial calendar has three distinct steps: the expected result for 2026, the 2027 Budget and the measures to be planned from 2028 for the financial consequences of the 2025 popular votes. The current improvement does not eliminate this sequence. ## How to follow the dossier The operational follow-up is primarily institutional. The Municipal Council has already approved the 2027 Budget, while the City Council must examine and approve it. To correctly interpret the next developments, it is useful to separate the procedure from the financial content and keep the different time horizons distinct.
### Five practical checks - 1. Check the status of the act: approval by the Municipal Council precedes examination and approval by the City Council. - 2. Separate 2027 from 2026: the former presents an expected deficit, while the latter shows a closing trend with a surplus in current operations. - 3. Read the multipliers by category: 80% concerns individuals, 85% legal entities. - 4. Assess investments and their financing together: 97 million net, 16,6 million in self-financing, and an overall result of minus 80,4 million. - 5. Keep the horizon open from 2028 onward: the Budget incorporates measures already decided, but not yet those needed to offset the financial consequences of the popular votes held in 2025.
This approach avoids two overly hasty interpretations. For a large group of employees, the stated effect is a reduction in weekly hours from 43 to 41, with no changes to the salary received. The text therefore links the reduction in hours to equal pay, without providing an individual quantification of the increase.
The new framework will cover the entire workforce, regardless of employment percentage. Even employees working less than 20% will benefit from the same guarantees and contractual conditions. In case of illness or injury, they will receive 100% of net salary for the first 90 days; thereafter, coverage will amount to 80% of gross salary.
### Purchasing power and wage measures
From January 1, 2027, the program will award employees ten Cumulus points for every franc spent across the entire range of Migros-branded supermarkets and in the group's self-service restaurants. The benefit will translate into an effective 10% discount on purchases, provided through shopping vouchers.
For 2027, Migros has planned an overall investment of 1.6% of the total payroll, including specific increases for individual companies. For Food Retail, the nationwide allocation reaches up to 0.3%; for other sectors, the ceiling may reach 0.7%. Individual subsidiaries will independently communicate how the measures will be implemented. For a cross-border worker employed by a group company, this is the concrete scope that can be gleaned from the announcement: hours, salary, protections, spending and communication from the subsidiary. The text does not indicate locations, the number of workers involved or separate rules based on residence. ## The comparison for those who work in the group
### Before and after, without conflating the different aspects
Before the new L-GAV, logistics, meat processing and the leisure sector were covered by specific agreements. The announcement describes their replacement and the adoption of uniform conditions company-wide. The correct comparison is therefore not only between the old and new number of hours: it also concerns the transition from sector-specific rules to a common framework.
The reduction from 43 to 41 hours is not presented as a universal measure for everyone. The source refers to a large group of employees. Therefore, a cross-border worker who works for Migros must interpret the application with reference to their own company and sector, without turning the general figure into an individual outcome that has already been defined. Pay remains unchanged for the group concerned.
The extension of guarantees to staff with an employment percentage below 20% broadens the contractual scope indicated in the announcement. The practical point here is the requirement described: according to the text, the employment percentage no longer excludes access to the same conditions. The same protection in the event of illness or accident is structured in two periods: 100% of net salary for the first 90 days and 80% of gross salary thereafter.
The Cumulus program should also be considered separately from the pay measure. It is presented as support for purchasing power: points accrue on the indicated purchases and the benefit comes in shopping vouchers. The investment of 1,6%, on the other hand, concerns the total payroll and includes the specific increases of the individual entities. In the text, it does not amount to an identical individual increase for everyone. Food Retail and the other sectors have different ranges, while the detailed implementation will be communicated by the subsidiaries.
For the cross-border worker reader, the scope must be kept narrow: the source does not mention Canton Ticino, the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax or double taxation. It therefore does not indicate any changes on these matters. The verifiable information remains the contractual information: hours, guarantees, spending and pay measures, with the level of detail deferred to the subsidiary. ## The employee's operational checklist
### Five steps to follow
1. Set the calendar. The new contract covers the 2027-2031 five-year period; for the Cumulus program, the date indicated is 1 January 2027. The source does not indicate any other individual deadlines, so the operational reference remains the one communicated by the group.
2. Identify the scope. Determine whether the employment relationship falls under logistics, meat processing, the leisure sector, Food Retail or the other company sectors. The new L-GAV supersedes the specific agreements for the first three sectors; the distinction also helps interpret the salary ranges indicated.
3. Wait for the communication from the subsidiary. The individual companies will independently and comprehensively communicate the implementation of the remuneration measures. This step connects the general framework to the situation of the individual employee, without adding percentages not reported in the announcement.
4. Compare working hours and protections. If you fall within the affected group, verify the reduction from 43 to 41 hours while maintaining the same salary. Also check access to the guarantees even with a working percentage below 20% and the sequence provided for illness or accident: 100% of net salary for 90 days, then 80% of gross salary.
5. Separate salary and spending. For 2027, note the overall investment of 1,6% of the total payroll, the allocation of up to 0,3% for Food Retail and up to 0,7% for the other sectors. For Cumulus, from 1 January 2027, consider ten points for every franc spent in Migros supermarkets and self-service restaurants, with an effective 10% discount in the form of shopping vouchers.
If you are a cross-border worker employed by a Migros company, this sequence allows you to read the communication without confusing the contract with matters not covered by the announcement. The source does not indicate forms, documents to submit or offices to contact: it is therefore not possible to derive any further procedure. The concrete step remains the independent communication from the subsidiary, to be compared with the conditions applicable to your employment relationship.

item.description: Lugano forecasts a deficit of 14,7 million The result improves by 4,8 million compared with the 2026-2033 plan The multipliers remain at 80% and 85% Investments
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Lugano forecasts a deficit of 14,7 million - The result improves by 4,8 million compared with the 2026-2033 plan - The multipliers remain at 80% and 85% - Planned net investments amount to 97 million
## Key facts - What → 2027 Budget - Deficit → 14,7 million francs - Multipliers → 80% individuals; 85% legal entities - Net investments → 97 million francs - Tax-funded requirement → 286,7 million francs
The Municipality of Lugano has approved the 2027 Budget and sent the report to the Municipal Council. A deficit of 14,7 million francs is forecast for current operations. The estimate is more favorable than the one previously formulated, but the financial recovery continues.
### Comparison with previous estimates
For 2027, the Financial Plan 2026-2033 indicated a deficit of 19,5 million: the current result is more favorable by 4,8 million. A previous multi-year projection indicated a deficit of 30,1 million, against which the gap reaches 15,4 million. The 2026 Budget, on the other hand, had estimated a deficit of 4,2 million.
On the tax front, the Municipality confirms the tax multipliers. For individuals, the multiplier is set at 80%, while for legal entities it stands at 85%. These are the same levels set for 2026, after a three-percentage-point increase for both categories.
Total planned net investments amount to 97 million francs and also include the balance for the purchase of PalaRaiffeisen, whose payment has been postponed. Ordinary expenses are estimated at 510,8 million, while ordinary revenues amount to 224,1 million; the tax-funded requirement is 286,7 million.
The document already incorporates the financial recovery measures adopted by the Municipality and requested by the Municipal Council. Excluded, however, are the measures that, starting in 2028, will have to neutralize the financial repercussions of the popular votes held in 2025.
Financial recovery continues to be a central issue in the political debate. Last June, the Management Commission had expressed divergent positions regarding the Financial Plan and the methods of financial recovery, including those relating to containing current expenditure and resorting to asset revaluations.
It was also announced at the presentation that the current financial year is trending toward closing with a surplus in current operations. The 2025 Final Accounts had closed the books with a surplus of 23,7 million, compared with a forecast deficit of 24 million; the result was largely due to extraordinary factors. ## For the cross-border commuter, what is the relevant figure
For those who work across the border and look at the finances of the Canton of Ticino, the message should be read as a document on the municipal budget of Lugano, not as a new individual rule. The figure of 14,7 million describes the City's current operations: it is neither an amount attributed to a cross-border commuter nor a figure that the source links to a single tax.
### The scope of the news
The only explicit tax-related figure is the confirmation of the municipal multipliers: 80% for individuals and 85% for legal entities. The correct comparison is therefore with 2026, when both had been increased by three points, not with a personal situation reconstructed without other information. The source does not provide taxable income, individual tax, municipality of residence or a calculation by taxpayer category. It therefore does not make it possible to estimate how the tax burden of an individual reader would change.
The message does not address permit G, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax or double taxation. For a cross-border commuter, this distinction is material: the text speaks of the City's financial consolidation and of covering the funding needs through taxes, but does not announce changes to these cross-border items.
| Item | Permitted interpretation | |---|---| | Current operating deficit | Overall result expected for 2027 | | Multipliers | Confirmed levels for individuals and legal entities | | Net investments | 97 million, with the PalaRaiffeisen balance deferred | | Financial consolidation | Measures already incorporated and new proposals expected |
The difference between the projections helps to convey the tone of the document. The expected deficit is smaller than in the two previous scenarios, but remains a deficit; it does not become a surplus merely because it is lower than 19,5 or 30,1 million. Likewise, the surplus expected for the current financial year does not eliminate the measures still to be defined from 2028 onward. The source in fact points to an estimated annual burden of 22,9 million and a rebalancing to be addressed over the 2028-2030 period. The cross-border commuter can therefore use the Budget to understand the trajectory of the City's finances, not to infer on their own the effects on cross-border taxation. ## How to follow the dossier without conflating different levels
For a cross-border worker who wants to understand whether the Budget contains an immediate consequence, the most prudent approach is to follow the process and keep the timeframes indicated in the message separate. The steps communicated make it possible to distinguish what has already been submitted from the measures that will be put forward later.
1. Start from the status of the act. The Municipality has approved the 2027 Budget and transmitted it to the Municipal Council. It is therefore advisable to distinguish the municipal approval from the transmission of the message, without attributing further decisions to the text. 2. Note the first deadline. By the end of the year, the Municipality will receive from the Financial Rehabilitation Committee proposals aimed at making municipal activities more efficient. The text describes these proposals as interventions concerning municipal activities and does not specify individual measures for cross-border workers. 3. Keep 2027 separate from what follows. During 2027, proposals aimed at reviewing the areas and priorities of the City's action will be presented. The measures to offset, starting in 2028, the financial effects of the popular votes held in 2025 are not yet included in the Budget. 4. This step helps distinguish the figures in the document from the measures still under discussion.
### What data can be used
For an orderly reading, it is advisable to note separately the projected deficit, the multipliers, net investments and the deadlines for the financial rehabilitation. It is not correct to add the expected result for the current financial year to the 2027 Budget, nor to use the 2025 Final Accounts as an automatic forecast: those accounts had closed with a surplus of 23,7 million, compared with a budgeted deficit of 24 million, largely due to extraordinary factors.
The source does not indicate forms, applications, personal documents or procedures to be submitted for a cross-border worker. The message therefore does not offer an individual simulation. If the goal is to turn the multiplier figure into a simulation of your own tax situation, use calcolatore fiscale.

item.title: ATA opposes the A2 Mendrisio‑Melano expansion
item.description: ATA opposes the expansion of the A2 between Mendrisio and Melano The project includes the Lenaccio viaduct and noise barriers PoLuMe envisages a third lane
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The ATA opposes the expansion of the A2 between Mendrisio and Melano - The project includes the Lenaccio viaduct and noise barriers - PoLuMe provides for a dynamic third lane during periods of heavy traffic - The association calls for new checks on noise and traffic
## Key facts - Who → ATA, Ticino section - Where → A2 motorway between Mendrisio and Melano - Measures → widening of the Lenaccio viaduct and noise barriers - Issue → emergency lane used as a dynamic third lane - Horizon → 2050 - Recipient → DATEC - Reference → Article 8 of the Noise Pollution Control Ordinance
## ATA's opposition
The planned measures include widening the Lenaccio viaduct and installing noise barriers. ATA disputes the assessments of the noise impact and the expected effects of increasing the motorway's capacity.
### The issue of the dynamic third lane
According to the association, the official documentation would not classify the measure as a substantial modification of the motorway. ATA disputes this interpretation, since the future PoLuMe project envisages using the emergency lane as a dynamic third lane during peak traffic hours. In its view, this solution would significantly increase the infrastructure's capacity and, consequently, traffic volumes. For the association, the measure should therefore be considered a substantial modification under Article 8 of the Noise Pollution Control Ordinance, with the consequences provided for environmental assessments.
### Noise, traffic and monitoring
The second front concerns noise emissions. ATA believes that the project's calculations are incorrect because they do not take into account the future construction of PoLuMe within the 2050 time horizon. It argues that the calculations omit both the use of the emergency lane as a dynamic third lane and the increase in traffic during certain time periods.
The association also disputes the report on the cantonal road: it would not include the data used to calculate its noise emissions, making it impossible to verify the traffic scenarios. The concerns also extend to noise protection, because the expansion of the road surface in use could reduce the effectiveness of the noise barriers. ATA therefore believes that a new assessment of the noise protection measures is needed.
The association identifies a tunnel as an alternative solution and calls for a new assessment of the increase in traffic. Finally, it fears that the increased motorway capacity will induce some users to return to cars, weakening the results achieved in recent years through the Canton's expansion of public transport. ## Why the third lane changes the interpretation of the project
For those travelling along the A2 between Mendrisio and Melano, the ATA's objection shifts attention from the visible work to the role that the stretch could assume during periods of heavy traffic. The viaduct and the noise barriers are elements of the project; the dynamic lane, on the other hand, is the element that, according to the association, changes capacity and traffic scenarios.
### Capacity is also an environmental variable
If the emergency lane is used as a dynamic third lane, the motorway is not assessed only in terms of its expanded surface area. The traffic volumes that the increase in capacity could generate also enter into the assessment. The ATA maintains that this phenomenon is also recognised by the Federal Roads Office (USTRA). For a user of the stretch, the practical issue therefore concerns not only the presence of the noise barriers, but also how the projected traffic is calculated during the different time periods.
The assessment for 2050 becomes the point of comparison between the scenario contained in the project and the one contested by the ATA. If PoLuMe, the third lane and increased traffic are missing from the calculations, the association believes that the picture does not represent the future situation made possible by the intervention. The same logic applies to the cantonal road: without the data used to calculate noise emissions, the scenarios could not be verified.
### Mobility and alternatives
The ATA's position combines the environment and modal choice. In its view, the increase in capacity could encourage a return to car use and undermine the results of the expansion of public transport carried out by the Canton in recent years. The proposed alternative is a tunnel, but the source does not describe its characteristics or route: its precise effect on traffic therefore cannot be determined.
The comparison remains between two interpretations: the official documentation, which does not consider the intervention a substantial modification, and the ATA's request to apply Article 8 OIF, redo the noise assessment and verify the effectiveness of the barriers. The consequence indicated by the source is a broader environmental assessment, not an outcome that has already been decided. ## How to follow the dossier
To read the dossier concretely, it is useful to separate what is already described in the project from the requests contained in the objection. The source documents the submission to DATEC, but does not report a subsequent decision. The informational task therefore consists in checking which assumptions enter into the assessments.
### Five points to check
1. Distinguish works and operations. On one side are the Lenaccio viaduct and the noise barriers; on the other, the use of the emergency lane as a third dynamic lane. 2. Check the time horizon. The assessment should be read in relation to 2050 and the future construction of PoLuMe. 3. Look for the data on the cantonal road. According to ATA, the report does not include those used for noise emissions; this is the point to verify in order to reconstruct the scenarios. 4. Assess the barriers in the expanded scenario. The effectiveness of the walls must be considered in light of the greater road surface used and the dynamic lane. 5. Compare mobility and alternatives. The dossier compares motorway capacity, the risk of a return to car use, the expansion of public transport by the Canton and the proposal for an alternative tunnel.
ATA's central request is twofold: to review the traffic forecasts and carry out a new assessment of the effectiveness of the noise protection measures. The reference invoked is Article 8 of the Noise Abatement Ordinance, while the addressee of the objection is DATEC. USTRA appears in the dossier in connection with recognition of the phenomenon of increased traffic linked to greater capacity.
This method avoids confusing a physical widening with the operational effect of the dynamic lane. It does not, however, make it possible to indicate schedules, diversions or works, because the source does not describe them. To follow the evolution of traffic conditions, consult storico traffico e code ai valichi.

item.title: Resignation from cross-border commuters: terms and steps in Ticino
item.description: Resignation from a job in Ticino: terms to be checked, impact on G permit, taxes, pension and unemployment for border workers.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Frontier Agreement in force from 1 January 2024 - Old frontier workers: exemption of €7,500 in the transition 2024–2033 - New frontier workers: deductible of €10,000 - Withholding tax withheld only in Switzerland
## Key facts - Agreement: signed on December 23, 2020 - Italian ratification: Law 83 of 13 June 2023 - Double taxation agreement: 9 March 1976 - Old cross-border commuters: already such before 17 July 2023 - KVG: right of option for cross-border commuters with G permit
From 1 January 2024 the New Cross-border Workers Agreement is in force. For a cross-border worker who works in the Canton of Ticino and resides in Italy, this date must be kept separate from the notice period: the first defines the framework of the agreement, the second governs the closure of the relationship according to the contract and the applicable rules.
The text was signed on 23 December 2020 and ratified in Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023. The correct reference, therefore, is not a new 2026 tax agreement: the indicated entry into force is 1 January 2024. The Italy-Switzerland Convention against double taxation was signed on 9 March 1976, while Switzerland is not a member of the EU or EEA.
When the relationship ends, the basic tax rule remains precise: on the cross-border worker's income, withholding tax is withheld only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit indicated in the EC framework of 730; it is therefore not an ordinary withholding tax in both countries.
### The term must be separated from the rest
Resignation, termination of the employment contract and the notice period are the first file to be closed. The date of communication and the date of termination should not be confused: before sending the communication, the cross-border worker must find the deadline from the contract and the applicable provisions. A date chosen without this verification may leave open the question of whether the relationship will actually end.
Then there are separate checks on the G permit, possible unemployment and the final pay slip. Added to these are AVS, LPP and KVG. The termination of the relationship must therefore be recorded separately for taxation, social security and health insurance, without automatically transforming one plan into the other.
Tax rates, including withholding tax and federal/cantonal rates, are established by federal and cantonal laws. At federal level they are administered by the AFC/ESTV and the cantonal tax administrations. UFAS, which concerns social security, and BFS, which collects statistical data, are not the bodies that set the rates. It is a useful step to avoid asking the wrong structure for a payroll check. ## How to read your pay slip and taxes after you resign
The most delicate part for a cross-border worker is not stopping at the last net salary. When checking documents, at least three levels must be separated: tax classification, Swiss contributions and health insurance. The reason for termination does not replace the dates that define the worker's category.
### The comparison between old and new cross-border workers
| Category | Time criterion | Rule indicated | |---|---|---| | Old cross-border workers | Already such before July 17, 2023 | Exemption €7'500; transitional regime 2024–2033 | | New cross-border workers | New regime | Deductible €10'000 |
The comparison serves to avoid applying the exemption of one category to another. A cross-border worker who was already a cross-border worker before 17 July 2023 must be read in the context of the old cross-border workers and the transitional period; for a new cross-border worker the figure to consider is the €10,000 deductible. The withholding tax on earned income remains on the Swiss side, while the credit in the EC framework of 730 is the Italian reference for avoiding double taxation.
Social security items have their own weight on a Swiss pay slip. The AVS/AI/IPG contributions payable by the employee are 5.3%; AD/AC is 1.1% up to a cap of CHF 148'200; LAINF is between 0.7% and 1.5%; LPP ranges from 7% to 18% by age group, from the 25th year. They are different percentages and should not be exchanged with withholding tax. Reading them separately helps not to confuse the final net with a single rate.
### KVG is not a tax item
KVG is health insurance, not the so-called 'health tax'. Cross-border workers with a G permit have the right of option; for adults the indicated deductibles range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. Even after notification of resignation, this item must be filed as insurance and not added to tax or social security rates.
The distinction avoids two practical errors: using the last payslip as a measure of the entire picture and confusing taxation with social security. For those who leave a job in the Canton of Ticino, the useful verification is therefore a statement with tax regime, AVS/LPP withholdings and KVG position, not a single statement of net income. ## Practice procedure before the last day
To make the termination of the employment contract orderly, the cross-border worker can work on a short sequence. The goal is to set the correct date and then deliver all information to the right chapter, without mixing contract, taxes, social security and insurance.
### Five checks before closing the relationship
1. Obtain the notice period. Read the contract and identify the applicable deadline. Put in writing, for personal use, the date of communication and the termination date calculated on the verified term. Do not replace this step with a generic figure found online.
2. Classify the tax position. Check if you were already a cross-border worker before 17 July 2023. This check separates the regime for old cross-border workers, with exemption of €7,500 and transitional period 2024–2033, from the €10,000 exemption provided for new cross-border workers.
3. Rebuild the tax part. Collect the information on the withholding tax withheld in Switzerland and prepare the reference to the tax credit of the EC framework of 730. For doubts about the rates, the correct perimeter is that of the federal and cantonal laws, the AFC/ESTV and the cantonal tax administrations.
4. Separate your pension from your paycheck. Read the AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF and LPP entries as different chapters. The employee must recognize the percentages and cap indicated for AD/AC, without adding them to the withholding tax or using them to estimate the net on their own.
5. Close administrative controls. The end of the relationship must be verified separately for the G permit and for any unemployment: you can consult the guide at Permesso G/B and that at disoccupazione frontalieri. On the healthcare level, it also retains the reference to the KVG option right and the applicable deductible.
Once these steps have been completed, the cross-border worker has a separate track for contract, taxation, social security, permit and health coverage. It's the most straightforward way to deal with a resignation without turning the end date into an automatic response about taxes or unemployment.

item.description: Friday, October 30, 2026 the Job Fair in Besano From 9 to 14 in the gym on Via Franzosi Organized by the Employment Center of Varese and the Municipality
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Friday, October 30, 2026, the Job Fair in Besano - From 9 to 14 at the gym on Via Franzosi - Organized by the Varese Employment Center and the Municipality - Direct interviews between companies and candidates
## Key facts - What: Valceresio Labour Fair - When: Friday, October 30, 2026, from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m. - Where: gym in Via Franzosi, Besano - Organisers: Centre for Employment of Varese and Municipality of Besano - Objective: to promote employment in the area
### A meeting between companies and candidates On Friday, October 30, 2026, the gym in Via Franzosi in Besano will host the first Valceresio Labour Fair. The appointment, scheduled from 9:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., was created to put local companies in direct contact with people looking for employment.
The Varese Employment Centre is organising the initiative together with the Municipality of Besano. The objective is to promote employment in the area, enhance local resources and put demand and supply of jobs in direct contact. The event will be held in the gym in Via Franzosi, which will bring together companies, candidates and guidance services during the morning.
The initiative is designed for those who enter the world of work for the first time, for those looking for a new job and for those who want to learn about other production companies. Participants will be able to meet the personnel managers of the companies present for a first cognitive interview; it is advisable to bring your CV with you.
The event is part of the employment dynamics of the area's borders. The proximity to the Canton of Ticino is recalled by the mayor of Besano as one of the elements that led the administration to promote the initiative. According to the reason expressed by the Municipality, there are still many people who, despite living near Switzerland, seek an employment capable of offering economic and personal satisfaction.
The Fair is therefore presented as a concrete alternative to cross-border opportunities alone. The project aims to give visibility to Valceresio companies and make it clearer which professionals they are looking for. For the Municipality, work and the territory can meet in the same place, through a day built around interviews and direct knowledge.
The source defines the event as the first event of its kind organised in Valceresio. Its local character concerns both companies called to present themselves, and people interested in finding a job or changing career path. The morning will therefore be dedicated to a direct discussion, without separating the moment of research from that of the presentation of the companies. ## The sectors and profiles sought
### From production to services The Fair will bring together opportunities related to various sectors of the local economy. The source mentions mechanical engineering, textiles, crafts, social and healthcare services, catering and manufacturing. These areas are accompanied by clerical and administrative services, with profiles requiring different skills and career paths.
The mechanical engineering sector includes, among the profiles sought, technical specialists, welders, machine tool operators, mechanical draftsmen, sheet metal workers, painters, tire technicians and maintenance technicians. The range therefore includes technical activities, specialized processing and maintenance-related duties.
The textile sector also offers several possibilities: the profiles listed include textile workers, seamstresses and pattern makers. In crafts and manufacturing, there are instead window and door installers, carpenters, surveyors, laborers and excavator operators. The list provided by the companies is not limited to a single qualification, but includes manual, technical and design-related work.
For administrative services, administrative and accounting clerks are sought. Catering includes bartenders and waiters, while the social and healthcare sector is looking for ASA and OSS workers. The simultaneous presence of these areas enables the event to appeal both to those with specific training and to those considering a new professional opportunity among very different sectors.
### The desks dedicated to work and business Alongside interviews with companies, two information and support desks are planned. The Varese Employment Center will set up a station to provide guidance on employment services. The same station will also offer practical assistance in reviewing and enhancing CVs, linking the search for employment with the preparation of documents to present to companies.
The Chamber of Commerce will participate in the Fair through the Punto Nuova Impresa desk. Citizens and aspiring entrepreneurs will be able to obtain information, guidance and advice on starting their own business or developing self-employment projects locally. The initiative, therefore, will not be aimed only at those seeking an interview as candidates, but also at those considering an independent career path.
### The provincial dimension The Province of Varese highlights the institutional work carried out in support of the community. The joint statement by President Marco Magrini and Provincial Councillor for Labour Carmelo Lauricella places the Besano Fair within the work carried out every year by the Province through the Labour Department and the Employment Centers.
According to the statement, this initiative aims to connect companies with people seeking employment in the various areas of the province. The presence of the provincial authority broadens the reach of the day, which nevertheless remains linked to Valceresio and the businesses operating in the area. ## The morning among booths and interviews
### The process for candidates and businesses The activities are concentrated in the morning of Friday, October 30. Participants will be able to bring their CV with them and speak directly with the personnel managers of the companies present during introductory interviews. No separate path is specified for each category: the Fair offers job seekers a space to connect with several businesses.
Besano's mayor, Leslie Giovanni Mulas, described how the initiative works as a simple flow through the booths: people will be able to walk among the stands, identify the companies of greatest interest, and sit down for an interview. The same setup offers businesses a broad audience of interested people, to whom they can introduce themselves and conduct the interviews needed to identify the employees they are seeking.
> “People who live in Besano and Valceresio must be able to count on job opportunities outside Switzerland as well.”
The mayor's statement sums up the local rationale for the event. Proximity to Canton Ticino is not presented as the only point of reference for people living in the area: the stated aim is to showcase local companies and make visible the professional profiles they are seeking. The interaction thus takes place in the same location, between those offering a job and those looking for employment.
For companies, the day is an opportunity to make themselves known directly and conduct interviews with an interested audience. For candidates, the program offers the chance to meet personnel managers without limiting themselves to reading a job advertisement. The CV becomes the starting point for direct contact, while the presence of different sectors broadens the opportunities for discussion available during the same morning.
Besano's administration considers this approach a first experience for Valceresio: work and the local area engage in dialogue, intersect, and can help each other prosper together. The event was specifically intended to create this link between people seeking employment and companies that need to clearly communicate the profiles they require.
The Municipality expressed its thanks to the Varese Employment Center for its support with the organization and to the Chamber of Commerce, which will be present for anyone who wants to register for VAT. The day will bring together interviews, guidance on employment services, and information on starting one's own business, while remaining rooted in the needs expressed by the area.

item.description: 2,87% in the third quarter in Ticino 3,31% forecast in the fourth quarter 2026 3,45% estimated in the first quarter 2027 Youth rate rising: 5,7% Seco rate
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 2,87% in the third quarter in Ticino - 3,31% forecast for the fourth quarter of 2026 - 3,45% estimated for the first quarter of 2027 - Youth rate increasing: 5,7%
## Key facts - Seco unemployment rate in Ticino → 2,87% - Fourth quarter of 2026 → 3,31% - First quarter of 2027 → 3,45% - Swiss residents → 2,2% - Female unemployment → 2,77% - Male unemployment → 2,9% - Share of women among the unemployed → 44,5% - Youth unemployment → 5,7%
The 2,87% recorded in Ticino in the third quarter of the year is the starting point of the latest update on Seco unemployment forecasts in Ticino, released by the Institute of Economic Research of the University of Italian Switzerland (Ire). The institute expects the rate to increase from now until the end of the year and also at the beginning of 2027.
The Ire model places the rate at 3,31% in the fourth quarter of 2026 and at 3,45% in the first quarter of 2027. These are the two time windows indicated for the expected growth: the final part of the current year and the beginning of the following year. The forecast concerns the Seco rate in Ticino and is presented as an estimate from the Ire model.
### The third-quarter picture
In the third quarter, the cantonal rate reached 2,87%, 0,3 percentage points higher year on year. Among Swiss residents, the rate was 2,2%, while among foreigners the figure was 4,17. The increase compared with the same period of the previous year was 0,2 percentage points for the former and 0,5 for the latter.
The gender breakdown shows a female unemployment rate of 2,77% and a male rate of 2,9%. The share of women among all unemployed people rose to 44,5% compared with the previous period, although it was down compared with that of last year. The youth unemployment figure, on the other hand, increased compared with the previous year and stood at 5,7%.
Ire, through the forecasts prepared by O-De, the Observatory of Economic Dynamics, therefore continues to indicate growth for both periods considered. The Usi institute nevertheless accompanies the figures with an explicit note of caution:
> The Usi institute specifies that, despite the usual caution in interpretation, the latest figures would appear to be higher than those of the previous year.
For the cross-border worker who works in Ticino, the figure to follow is therefore the overall evolution of the cantonal rate over the two quarters indicated. The source does not add an individual forecast, but makes the expected direction of the regional labor market clear. For a cross-border worker, the update provides an indicator of the labor market in Canton Ticino, but not an individual decision. The source covers aggregate rates and a forecasting model; it does not indicate how many employment relationships will change, which professions will be involved, or which people will lose their jobs. This distinction avoids reading 3,31% or 3,45% as a personal forecast.
### Three comparisons to keep separate
The first comparison concerns residence. In the report, Swiss and foreign residents have different values and also different annual increases. For a cross-border worker, however, the source does not say that the figure for foreign residents automatically coincides with that for cross-border workers. That overlap is not contained in the update and should not be added to the interpretation.
The second comparison is between rate and composition. The female and male rates measure two distinct values; the 44,5% share, on the other hand, describes the presence of women among all unemployed people. It is therefore not a second female rate, but a composition indicator referring to the previous period and compared with that of last year.
The third comparison concerns young people. The 5,7% is accompanied by the indication that the rate increased compared with the previous year. The text does not cross-reference this figure with residence or gender: it therefore does not make it possible to derive a specific value for young foreign residents, women, or cross-border workers.
The text does not address the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, tax rebates, INPS, or double taxation. Consequently, these elements cannot automatically be linked to the Ire forecast: the bulletin does not indicate changes in taxation, social security, health insurance, or procedures for cross-border workers.
The time comparison remains. The estimates for the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2027 signal an expected direction, accompanied by the institute’s caution. For those who work in Ticino, they are therefore a reference for the general trend in unemployment, not a calculation of their own employment risk. To follow the figure without attributing more meaning to it than is contained in the source, a cross-border worker can use a brief reading procedure. The aim is to distinguish the observed figure, future estimates and the categories used by Ire.
### Four steps
1. Start with the period observed. Record the third quarter as the basis for comparison and note the 2,87% Seco rate in Ticino. Keep this value separate from the two future estimates.
2. Separate residence. Report 2,2% for Swiss residents and 4,17 for foreign residents, together with the annual increases of 0,2 and 0,5 percentage points. Do not combine the two indicators into a single figure.
3. Keep gender, composition and age distinct. The values 2,77% and 2,9% are the female and male rates; 44,5% is the share of women among the total unemployed; 5,7% is the youth rate. They are different lines in the reading.
4. Place the two estimates on the calendar: 3,31% for the fourth quarter 2026 and 3,45% for the first quarter 2027. Next to both, note that Ire recommends caution and identifies them as values higher than those of the previous year.
This method prevents using a cantonal forecast as if it were the result of a single position and confusing a rate with a share of the total. The source allows comparison between the periods and groups indicated, but not a personal calculation.
If the question concerns the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, rebates, INPS or double taxation, this source does not provide data, deadlines, documents, rates or operational steps on these topics. It is therefore not possible to derive an administrative procedure for the cross-border worker from Ire’s figures.
To follow the topic, consult section Disoccupazione frontalieri.

item.title: Migros: new CCL from 2027, 10% discount
item.description: Migros’ national CCL will be in force from 2027 to 2031: uniform conditions, a 41-hour workweek for many, and a 10% discount with shopping vouchers.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - National CCL in force from 2027 to 2031 - 10% discount with shopping vouchers - Same conditions even below 20% employment - After 90 days: 80% of gross salary
## Key facts - Duration → 2027-2031 - Purchases → 10% discount with shopping vouchers - Employment → same conditions even below 20% - Working hours → 41 hours instead of 43 for many employees - Illness or accident → full net pay for 90 days, then 80% of gross pay
From 2027 to 2031, the new national collective labor agreement for Migros will be in force. The company indicates better conditions for employees, with measures concerning shopping, working hours, and payment in the event of illness or accident.
The most immediate benefit concerns purchases: employees will be able to shop with a 10% discount through shopping vouchers. The source does not specify an amount for the vouchers, nor does it describe the procedure by which they will be distributed or used. The verifiable information is therefore the discount percentage and its connection to the shopping vouchers.
The CCL will apply regardless of the employment percentage. Those working at a percentage below 20% will also benefit from the same conditions. For a cross-border worker employed by Migros, this is the part to read most carefully in their employment relationship: the criterion indicated is the employment percentage, not a different threshold described in the text.
### Working hours and income protection
Regarding working hours, the company emphasizes that many employees will move to 41 hours per week instead of 43, while maintaining the same salary. The wording concerns many employees, does not establish that the reduction applies to everyone, and does not indicate which positions are included.
Benefits in the event of illness or accident will also be uniform. Full net salary will be paid for a maximum of 90 days; subsequently, 80% of gross salary will be paid. The distinction between net and gross is an essential part of the measure: the text does not permit converting 80% gross into a net figure or extending the first period beyond 90 days.
When reading the payslip, the source therefore provides two different and consecutive references: net pay for the first phase and gross pay for the subsequent one. No absolute amount is indicated, and it is not explained how the employer will operationally implement the transition; these elements remain outside the available text.
The connection with cross-border work remains limited to the employment conditions at Migros. The source does not indicate locations, employee numbers, or specific details for Canton Ticino: it presents the CCL as national and sets its validity from 2027 to 2031. ## How to read the change as a cross-border worker
For a cross-border worker employed by Migros, the new CCL should be read as a change to the employment conditions, not as information about all aspects of cross-border work. The source limits the changes to four elements: discount on purchases, employment level, weekly hours, and benefits in the event of sickness or an accident.
### The practical comparison
| Item | Indication of the new CCL | |---|---| | Purchases | 10% discount via shopping vouchers | | Employment level | same conditions even below 20% | | Hours | 41 hours instead of 43 for many employees, with the same salary | | Sickness or accident | full net salary for up to 90 days, then 80% of gross salary |
The table helps avoid confusing different measures. The 10% concerns purchases and is linked to shopping vouchers; the text does not describe it in other terms. The 20% threshold concerns the application of the CCL conditions, and the source does not add any other thresholds. The change from 43 to 41 hours applies to many employees, while the salary remains the same for those covered by the measure indicated by the company.
The section on absences also requires a separate reading. During the first period, the reference is the full net salary, with a maximum limit of 90 days. After that limit, the reference changes: 80% is calculated on the gross salary, according to the source's wording. Without an individual salary figure, the text makes it possible to clarify the rule, but not to calculate a personal amount.
To avoid overinterpretation, the scope must be kept narrow. The source does not mention a G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, tax rebates, or double taxation. These matters therefore cannot be presented as having been changed by the CCL described.
For the cross-border worker, the useful information is the separation between the contractual level and other topics: here, the subject is the conditions offered by Migros to employees, without additional information on taxation, social security, health insurance, or commuting. ## Checklist for the 2027-2031 period
A Migros cross-border employee can turn the information in the CCL into a simple check, without adding data not provided by the text. The objective is to distinguish what is already defined from what remains to be specified.
### Five practical checks
1. Check the percentage of work. If the percentage is below 20%, the new CCL indicates access to the same conditions. The relevant reference is that of the employment relationship. 2. Compare the weekly hours. Check whether the position is among those of the many employees for whom 41 hours rather than 43 are indicated. The comparison must keep the corresponding salary data alongside it. 3. Separate out the shopping benefit. Record that the discount is 10% and that the source links it to shopping vouchers. The text does not indicate amounts, delivery methods or the duration of the vouchers, so these details should not be reconstructed. 4. Note the two phases in the event of absence. In the event of illness or accident, the first reference is the full net salary for a maximum of 90 days. After that, 80% of the gross salary applies. Keeping the two references separate avoids comparing net and gross as if they were the same item. 5. Note the time window. The CCL will be in force from 2027 to 2031, but the source does not indicate the precise start day or an individual procedure. The certain data to use is therefore the stated interval, not an invented calendar deadline.
This checklist does not expand the content of the agreement. The source does not link the measures to external tax or social-security matters and does not describe individual procedures for employees. For the cross-border reader, the check thus remains anchored to the working conditions indicated by Migros.
After collecting the percentage, hours and salary references, you can organize the comparison between gross and net with simulatore busta paga.
*Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/s/4164916)*
